# Contributing to Red Socket

Thanks for helping out. These guidelines apply to every Red Socket repository unless the repository has its own.

## Reporting bugs and suggesting features

Open an issue in the project's repository and pick **Bug report** or **Feature request**. For bugs, the log and the exact versions you use help the most.

Please search the open issues first. If someone has already reported the same thing, add what you know to that issue instead.

## Our approach

Our mods keep the game's rules as they are and take out the waiting, the repeated clicks and the small accidents. Ideas that fit that are the most likely to be added. Every feature can be turned off, so new features need an option to turn them off too.

## Pull requests

1. For anything bigger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach before you spend time on it.
2. Fork the repository and make your change on a new branch.
3. Follow the style of the code around your change, and the repository's `.editorconfig` if it has one.
4. Test your change in the game.
5. Open a pull request and fill in the template.

## Translations

Translations are welcome. Each mod's README explains how to add a language, for example the [SDV++ translation guide](https://github.com/red-socket/sdvpp#translations).

## Code of conduct

Everyone taking part is expected to follow our [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
